newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 8.

text.p: Some police say they are frustrated by having to deal with the increasing number of psychiatric and intellectually disabled patients being discharged. Ninety-one intellectually disabled people from Porirua Hospital had been discharged since March 1995, the Central Coast Health said on Tuesday. Senior Sergeant Steve Whitehead, of Porirua, said concerned police were having to deal with what was essentially a health problem. Page 1.

The office of the parliamentary commissioner for the environment was underfunded, the commissioner, Morgan Williams, said after he was sworn in on Tuesday. Williams, who replaces Helen Hughes who retired last year, said he would be pushing for an increase in the $1.8 million the office gets. Page 2.

The diplomatic corps will attend the official Waitangi Day function at Government House in Wellington next month and will not attend ceremonies at Waitangi. The dean of the corps, Chilean ambassador Demetrio Infante, said diplomats had been invited by Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys to a
cocktail party at Government House on Waitangi Day. An invitation from the highest authority in New Zealand meant diplomats had no choice but to attend, Infante said. Page 3.

The sharemarket continued its bullish start to 1997 on Tuesday as it went through the 2,400 mark for the first time since February 1994. A late rally saw the NZSE 40 index close 11 points up at 2408.28 on turnover of $40.3 million. But brokers tempered any euphoria with a warning that the market could be benefiting from the "January effect" and that some stocks were running ahead of themselves. ANZ Securities managing director
Tim Preston said the market had benefited from a solid Wall Street. Page 13.

A significant fall in the New Zealand dollar is unlikely this year as the economy grows more strongly than most expect, according to Bankers Trust. It said economic growth bottomed in the last quarter of 1996 and would accelerate after an easing in monetary conditions that should continue through the current quarter. The continuing stimulus of last year's tax cuts, more government spending from the middle of the year, and the government's commitment to the existing economic framework would
also push growth. That was the consensus view. Page 13.

Brierley Investments has been forced to ringfence its Air New Zealand A shares to avoid an enforced selldown of the stake now that it is no longer a New Zealand company. BIL has been removed from the Overseas Investment Commission's exemption schedule, making it a foreign company. Companies listed on the schedule are exempted from the Overseas Investment Regulations 1995. Page 13.

Union Shipping and Australia and New Zealand Direct had formed a new company to operate trans-Tasman and North American services, the two groups said on Tuesday. The new company is a result of an agreement between Union Shipping's 50 percent shareholder Brierley Investments and ANZDL's owner, Groupe Bollore Technologies. Page 13.

Direct Capital Partners has taken a 44.5 percent stake in Airwork NZ. Direct Capital paid $12 million for its stake, leaving Airwork managing director Hugh Jones with 55.5 percent. Direct Capital chief executive Ross George said Airwork would
use the capital to "target further growth opportunities in airfreight and aircraft maintenance and to retire existing debt". Page 13.
